text:
maya: quick sync — I pushed a bring-up of speculative decoding on the new quant-14b candidate (int8/ntk-aware). observed ~1.6x median token throughput improvement in our toy harness, but some quality falloff on the longform evals. wanted to surface early numbers and get ops/input on measurement plan.

sam: nice. what harness + batch settings? any drift in unquantized baseline? :thinking:

maya: harness = local bench runner (bench_v2), seq_len=1024, beamless sampling, batch=8 on a single A100. baseline is fp16 model we had last week. numbers: median latency/token 12.4ms -> 7.8ms with speculative (prefetch+early-accept), p50 throughput +60%-ish.

maya: quality: on redwood-openqa and convQA sets, EM dropped ~1.8 pts and F1 ~1.2 pts. on commonsense-cloze the drop is smaller (~0.4 pts). perplexity on validation increased from 11.2 -> 11.9.

ed: are you sure it's decode path only? could the quantized weights + kernel selection be inflating KL? Did you run identical RNG/seed?

maya: good call — I re-ran with fixed RNG and matched kernel selection as much as possible. difference persists. suspect it's interaction between early-accept heuristic and quantized logits smoothing.

ricardo: can you paste the speculative config you used? especially the acceptance threshold and async prefetch window.

maya: pasted below:

```
speculative: true
accept_threshold: 0.65   # prob mass for early accept
prefetch_window: 6
kv_cache_mode: staged
quant_profile: int8-ntk-aware
```

sam: acceptance at 0.65 seems aggressive for quantized logits — quant noise can concentrate mass differently. try 0.75 or add a tiny temperature bump for candidate scoring.

ed: also check top-k/top-p changes between fp16 and int8 implementations. quant rounding can make tail behavior jumpier which hurts exact-match metrics even if human-readable output seems fine.

maya: noted. quick ablation I ran: keep accept_threshold=0.65 but add `post_quant_temp=1.05` -> EM drop narrows to ~0.8 pts. throughput still +45% vs baseline.

ricardo: interesting. do we have token-level KL / calibration plots between runs? that will tell if speculation systematically biases next-token distribution.

maya: have token-KL for 2k prompts, attaching inline snapshot (summary): mean token-KL increased 0.018 nat/token, tail (95th) up 0.09. sounds small but could push exact-match.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2 -> started on prod-canary cluster (canary id=cd-7319). Monitoring: latency p95, token errors, OOMs.

sam: for gating, propose: run controlled A/B on 10k diverse prompts (wiki qa, conv, longform, code), collect EM/F1, token-KL, and a small human eval on 500 samples. include both accept_threshold=0.65 and 0.75 arms, plus baseline.

maya: agreed. I'll queue the A/B. timeline: bench -> offline A/B -> small human batch. target to have preliminary results tomorrow EOD.

ed: also log `chosen_path` for each step (early_accept vs full-decode) and the quantized kernel id, so we can correlate failures to kernel selection.

maya: adding that to the run — good idea.

ricardo: another non-obvious point: tokenization boundary effects. quantized logits + early accept might prefer shorter tokens, slightly changing segmentation on ambiguous cases. please include detokenized diff examples in the triage set.

maya: will do. will also throw in a simple regen test (5-beam greedy regen) to see if outputs are recoverable via reroll.

sam: one more operational ask — keep a quick revert plan: disable speculative flag and fallback to fp16 model on canary if EM drops >1.5 pts on the A/B. ops-bot, make sure rollback script is ready.

ops-bot: rollback script present at `infra/deploy/scripts/rollback_speculative.sh`. Canary alert TTL = 2h.

maya: thanks all. I'll post the A/B run id + short summary once it's done. for now, conservative tweak: try accept_threshold=0.72 + post_quant_temp=1.03 on next run.

sam: perfect. small doc request — please capture the eval sampling seeds + exact prompt files in the run metadata. reproducibility is key here.

maya: yup. metadata saved. will ping here with run id. :thumbsup:
